text:
Both emails are short and cover the three requested areas: data analysis, presentation style, and clarity of conclusions.

Assistant A is missing a subject line and uses a casual "Hi" and a run-together sign-off ("Thanks, <your name>"). It also assumes details the user never gave ("for the finance team", "The report is attached"). The tone is less professional, and the formatting is rough, with no clear paragraphs or sign-off line.

Assistant B is more polished and professional. It has a proper greeting, a clear request, and a courteous close. It also invents nothing. It does not include a subject line either, and "Dear" with "Sincerely" is somewhat formal. It does phrase the request more smoothly, working the three areas into one sentence.

Overall, B is better in professionalism and formatting. A's mention of an attachment is practical, but the unsupported assumptions and weaker structure count against it.

[[B]]
